questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
options: A new drug that slows early-stage Alzheimer's progression
How practicing tongue twisters can improve older adults' memory
Commercial phone apps that diagnose Parkinson's from voice
Using subtle speech changes to predict and track dementia risk
questions.explain: Researchers analyze speech features to predict dementia risk and track brain health.

questions.q: In Dr. Eshghi's 49-person study, how accurate was the speech-based analysis at best?
options: 77 percent
90 percent
47 percent
62 percent
questions.explain: Speech analysis classified participants up to 77 percent accurately versus 47 percent for cognitive testing models.

questions.q: What does the SpeechDX study collect?
options: Three years of speech data from 2,000 people in three countries
Two years of speech data from 1,000 people across Europe alone
One year of speech data from 500 people in the United States
Five years of speech data from 49 people in the Boston area
questions.explain: SpeechDX collects three years of speech data, plus blood tests and scans, for 2,000 people in the U.S., Australia and Spain.

questions.q: What did Deb's second assessment show compared with two years earlier?
options: Her vocabulary shrank and her speech became noticeably more monotone
She paused more often and her average pitch was slightly higher
She was reclassified as moderate-risk after her blood levels rose
She spoke noticeably faster, with fewer pauses and a lower pitch
questions.explain: She paused more, spent more time pausing, had slightly higher pitch, and remained cognitively unimpaired.

questions.q: What would Dr. Au likely say about commercial speech analysis apps?
options: They are more accurate than brain scans or spinal taps
They are already ready for use in routine health care
They need more evidence before use in health care
They should replace blood tests as a screening tool
questions.explain: She said it is not ready for prime time in the health care space and more data is needed.
